column1: # One line of OCaml per row, after the verdict the pattern of the column state must give it.
# count: the line creates or changes mutable state, whatever its scope. skip: it does not.
# The lexer's lexbuf counts where it is made: it is made for one file, but it is
# mutable, as a local ref cell is. Calls that change it later (Lexing.new_line,
# the rules of the lexer) do not count, as Buffer.add_string does not.
